notice: A typical topic progression for orientation only; not a binding curriculum mapping for any German state.

subtopics.label: Reading distance-time graphs
subtopics.learning_goal: Read speed as the steepness of a distance-time graph and compare two motions by their lines.
misconceptions: The graph is read as a picture of the path, so a rising line is taken for going uphill.
A higher line is called faster, even where a lower line is steeper.

subtopics.label: Calculating speed
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate speed as distance divided by time and state the result with its unit.
misconceptions: Distance and time are divided the wrong way round.
The result is stated without a unit, so metres per second and kilometres per hour blur together.

subtopics.label: Recognising uniform motion
subtopics.learning_goal: Decide from a distance-time graph whether a motion is uniform and justify it from the straightness of the line.
misconceptions: Any rising line is called uniform, even where it visibly bends.
A resting phase is read as the object moving backwards.

subtopics.label: Forces as arrows
subtopics.learning_goal: Represent a force as an arrow whose direction and length state where it acts and how strongly.
misconceptions: The arrow is drawn from where the force comes from instead of on the body it acts on.
Arrow length is treated as decoration rather than as the size of the force.

subtopics.label: Balanced and unbalanced forces
subtopics.learning_goal: Decide whether the forces on a body balance and predict whether its motion changes.
misconceptions: A moving body is assumed to need a constant force to keep moving.
Balanced forces are taken to mean the body must be at rest.

subtopics.label: Reading velocity-time graphs
subtopics.learning_goal: Read acceleration as the steepness of a velocity-time graph and tell speeding up from slowing down.
misconceptions: A velocity-time graph is read as a distance-time graph, so a flat line is taken for standing still.
A falling line is read as moving backwards instead of slowing down.

subtopics.label: Calculating acceleration
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate acceleration as the change in velocity divided by the time taken, with its unit.
misconceptions: The final velocity is used instead of the change in velocity.
The unit is written as metres per second, dropping the second division by time.

subtopics.label: Forms of energy and transfers
subtopics.learning_goal: Name the main forms of energy and describe a transfer chain for one everyday process.
misconceptions: Energy is said to be used up rather than transferred to another form.
Energy is treated as a substance an object contains rather than a quantity that is accounted.

subtopics.label: Kinetic and potential energy
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate kinetic and gravitational potential energy for simple cases and compare the results.
misconceptions: Doubling the speed is expected to double the kinetic energy instead of quadrupling it.
Height is measured from the ground even when the task sets a different reference level.

subtopics.label: Mechanical work
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate mechanical work as force times distance along the direction of the force.
misconceptions: Holding a heavy bag still is counted as doing mechanical work.
Force and distance are multiplied even when they point in different directions.

subtopics.label: Power
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate power as work divided by time and interpret the watt as one joule per second.
misconceptions: Power and energy are used interchangeably, as household bills often do.
A larger force is assumed to always mean more power, regardless of speed.
